'''''Vicia bithynica'''''<ref name=Stace>[[C. A. Stace]], ''New Flora of the British Isles'', 4th edition 2019. {{ISBN|978-15272-2630-2}}.</ref> known as '''Bithynian vetch''', is a species of flowering plant in the bean family [[Fabaceae]]. It was described by [[Carl Linnaeus]], initially as ''Lathyrus bithynicus'' (as a type of pea) but later moved to the genus ''Vicia'' (vetches).<ref name=Sell>{{cite book |last1=Sell |first1=Peter |last2=Murrell |first2=Gina |title=Flora of Great Britain and Ireland, vol 3 |date=2009 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge |isbn=978-0-521-55337-7}}</ref> The specific name is derived from [[Bithynia]], an ancient kingdom situated on the north coast of [[Anatolia]], in modern day [[Turkey]].

==Description==
An annual with climbing stems, scrambling or climbing to about 60 cm tall. The leaves are arranged alternately along the stem, are up to about 9 cm long, have 2–3 pairs of leaflets, and end in branched tendrils. The [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]]s are 2 cm long with a large, ovate, dentate [[stipule]] at the base. The flowers are arranged in pairs (although sometimes solitary) on long (5 cm) [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncles]] branching from the leaf axils. The petals are purple and white, 2 cm long, and have 10 [[stamen]]s and 1 [[stigma (botany)#style|style]]. The fruit is a hairy pod or [[legume]] up to 5 cm long with 4 to 8 seeds.<ref name=Stace/> It has 14 chromosomes.<ref name=Stace/><ref name=Başbağ>{{cite journal |last1=Başbağ |first1=Mehmet |title=Vicia taxa in the Flora of Turkey |journal=Anadolu Tarım Bilim. Derg. |date=2013 |volume=28 |page=59.66 |doi=10.7161/anajas.2013.281.59 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/253234474|doi-access=free }}</ref>

''Vicia bithynica'' is not cultivated for human or livestock consumption. The seeds contain high levels of [[vicine]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Griffith |first1=D.W. |title=The Concentration of Vicine and Convicine in Vicia faba and some Related Species and their Distribution within Mature Seeds |journal=J. Sci. Food Agric. |date=1992 |volume=59 |issue=4 |pages=463–468 |doi=10.1002/jsfa.2740590406 |url=https://fr.art1lib.org/book/1695024/793219 |url-access=subscription |archive-date=2022-01-23 |access-date=2022-01-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220123104526/https://fr.art1lib.org/book/1695024/793219 |url-status=dead }}</ref> which causes [[Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency|favism]] amongst susceptible individuals.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Warren |first1=Susan |title=The Wild Flowers of Skopelos |url=http://wildflowersofskopelos.org.uk/Purple_mauve/Pages/Vicia_bithynica.html}}</ref>

==Habitat==
The habitat of ''V. bithynica'' is often described as 'woodland and scrub' but Bennett & Maxted<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bennett |first1=S.J. |last2=Maxted |first2=N. |title=An ecogeographic analysis of the ''Vicia narbonensis'' complex |journal=Genetic Resources and Crop Evolution |date=1997 |volume=44 |issue=5 |pages=411–428|doi=10.1023/A:1008688919569 |s2cid=2863256 }}</ref> examined many [[herbarium]] specimens for habitat data and concluded that it was most common in [[calcareous grassland]], while others<ref>{{cite book |last1=Van de Wouw |first1=M. |chapter=Vetches (Vicia L.) |editor-last1=Maxted |editor-first1=N. |editor-last2= Bennett |editor-first2=S.J. |title=Plant Genetic Resources of Legumes in the Mediterranean |publisher=Springer, Dordrecht |date=2001 |series=Current Plant Science and Biotechnology in Agriculture |volume=39 |pages=134–158 |doi=10.1007/978-94-015-9823-1_8 |isbn=978-90-481-5613-9 |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-94-015-9823-1_8}}</ref> describe it as a weed of agricultural fields. In Greece, it is a native [[therophyte]] of dry scrub ([[phrygana]]) and [[grassland]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Dimopoulos |first1=Panayotis |title=Vascular plants of Greece: An annotated checklist |date=2013 |url=https://portal.cybertaxonomy.org/flora-greece/cdm_dataportal/taxon/93e2ea6c-ad12-43c3-ba43-6dd569f76da1}}</ref>

In Britain, at the northern extremity of its range, it is considered to be a plant of coastal undercliffs, the backs of beaches, bare ground, hedges and old railway lines.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Stewart |first1=A. |last2=Pearman |first2=D.A. |last3=Preston |first3=C.D. |title=Scarce Plants in Britain |date=1994 |publisher=JNCC |location=Peterborough |isbn=1-873701-66-7}}</ref>

==Distribution==
''Vicia bithynica'' is widespread around the Mediterranean and in Europe as far north as [[Scandinavia]], and there are isolated populations in the [[Azores]], United States, Australia and New Zealand.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Global Biodiversity Information Facility |title=''Vicia bithynica'' (L.) L. |url=https://www.gbif.org/species/2975309}}</ref>

It is common in [[Turkey]] and considered to be native there,<ref name=Başbağ/> as it is in [[Malta]],<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mifsud |first1=Stephen |title=Vicia bithynica (Bithynian Vetch) |url=https://www.maltawildplants.com/FABC/Vicia_bithynica.php |website=Malta Wild Plants}}</ref> becoming rarer further north. In Britain it is classified as Vulnerable<ref>{{cite book |last1=Cheffings |first1=C. |title=The Vascular Plant Red Data List for Great Britain |date=2005 |publisher=JNCC |location=Peterborough}}</ref> and is declining in abundance,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Biological Records Centre |title=Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora |url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/vicia-bithynica |access-date=2022-01-20 |archive-date=2022-01-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220120202957/https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/vicia-bithynica |url-status=dead }}</ref> although it is protected in several [[site of special scientific interest|sites of special scientific interest]] such as [[Sheppey Cliffs and Foreshore]] and [[Swanscombe Peninsula]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Natural England |title=Swanscombe Peninsula Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), confirmation of notification |url=https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1031169/board-paper-nebpu-106-01.pdf}}</ref>
